ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Fake or Fact, That Is the Question

fullPassage:
Fake or Fact, That Is the Question

British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. He created a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and wrote it was reservations only. He did this to make people think The Shed was a special restaurant.

He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site.

Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks."

Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks.

Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows.

If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully considered information about The Shed without being distracted by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more credible media. If they had done these things, they would likely have suspected that something was not right.

Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage. However, false information can cause emotional or financial harm to people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can stir up hatred against that group. It can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, misleading online reviews about questionable products often trick people into wasting money.

To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of critically evaluating what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Look at the website the story comes from. Does it look real? Are there spelling errors? Does it have other stories or just the one you read? Check that the story contains references and links to other information. Click on those links and see if the other information looks reliable. Websites with false information often do not have many real stories about other topics. They also often have lots of advertisements that pop up when you visit the sites.

You should then check the credibility of the content creator. If a story has no writer's name, this could be a sign that its content is questionable. If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before. If the person has not written anything else or writes for a website that looks unreliable, think twice before believing the content.

Finally, check who else is reporting the story. If no other media are reporting the same story, the story may not be true. Pick a few keywords from the story and put them in a search site to see if other media are supporting the story.

Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.

questions.passage: British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. He ①<u>created</u> a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and ②<u>writing</u> it was reservations only. He did this to ③<u>make</u> people think The Shed was a ④<u>special</u> restaurant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② writing → wrote. 'did not provide ... and wrote'에서 and로 연결된 병렬 구조. 과거시제 동사 wrote가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ② writing: and 앞의 did not provide와 병렬. 과거시제 wrote 필요. writing(현재분사)은 동사 역할 불가.
❌ ① created: 과거시제. He created — 올바름.
❌ ③ make: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형(think). 올바름.
❌ ④ special: 형용사로 명사 restaurant 수식. 올바름.
det.tip: and로 연결된 병렬 구조에서는 동사 시제가 일치해야 한다. did not provide and wrote (O) / did not provide and writing (X).

questions.passage: To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that ①<u>enable</u> us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or ②<u>deceives</u> people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be ③<u>influential</u>, as The Shed incident ④<u>showing</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ showing → shows. 독립절의 동사 자리로, 현재시제 shows가 와야 한다. as The Shed incident shows = The Shed 사건이 보여주듯이.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ showing: as절의 주어 The Shed incident 뒤 동사 자리. shows(현재시제) 필요.
❌ ① enable: 선행사 attitude and knowledge(복수) — 복수 동사 enable. 올바름.
❌ ② deceives: information that deceives — 3인칭 단수. 올바름.
❌ ③ influential: be influential — 보어. 올바름.
det.tip: as S V 구문에서 V는 반드시 서술동사 형태. as the incident shows (O) / as the incident showing (X).

questions.passage: If people had been digitally literate, they would not have been fooled by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully ①<u>considered</u> information about The Shed without ②<u>being distracted</u> by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not ③<u>appear</u> in other more ④<u>credibly</u> media.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ credibly → credible. 명사 media를 수식하는 자리이므로 형용사 credible이 와야 한다. credibly는 부사.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ credibly: more ___ media — 명사 앞 형용사 자리. credible(형용사) 필요. credibly(부사) 불가.
❌ ① considered: would have considered — 가정법 과거완료. 올바름.
❌ ② being distracted: without being distracted — 전치사 + 동명사 수동. 올바름.
❌ ③ appear: did not appear — 부정 과거. 올바름.
det.tip: more + 형용사 + 명사 구조: more credible media (O). 부사 credibly는 동사/형용사 수식에만 사용.

questions.passage: He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write ①<u>favorable</u> fake reviews on the review site. Things quickly got "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts, The Shed continuously ②<u>declined</u> the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls ③<u>requesting</u> reservations. Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully ④<u>booked</u> for the next six weeks."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② declined → climbed. 원문: 'The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings.' 최하위에서 순위가 올라갔다는 맥락에서 declined(하락했다)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ② declined: 원문은 climbed(올라갔다). 최하위에서 순위 상승 맥락에 declined(하락) 부적절.
❌ ① favorable: 원문 그대로(호의적인).
❌ ③ requesting: 원문 그대로(요청하는).
❌ ④ booked: 원문 그대로(예약된).
det.tip: climbed(올라갔다) ↔ declined(하락했다). from the lowest → climbed = 최하위에서 상승.

questions.passage: To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of critically ①<u>evaluating</u> what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Check that the story contains references and links to other information. Click on those links and see if the other information looks ②<u>reliable</u>. Websites with false information often do not have many ③<u>real</u> stories about other topics. They also often have lots of advertisements that ④<u>disappear</u> when you visit the sites.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ disappear → pop up. 원문: 'advertisements that pop up when you visit the sites.' 광고가 사라지는 것이 아니라 팝업으로 뜬다는 맥락에서 disappear(사라지다)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ disappear: 원문은 pop up(팝업으로 뜨다). 가짜 사이트의 광고가 사라진다는 것은 맥락 부적절.
❌ ① evaluating: 원문 그대로(평가하는).
❌ ② reliable: 원문 그대로(신뢰할 수 있는).
❌ ③ real: 원문 그대로(진짜).
det.tip: pop up(팝업으로 뜨다) ↔ disappear(사라지다). 가짜 사이트 = 광고가 많이 뜸.

questions.passage: Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to __________ information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디지털 기술을 사용하여 정보를 찾고, 평가하고, 만들고, 전달하는 능력이 디지털 리터러시이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ find, evaluate, create, and communicate: 원문 직접 인용. 정보를 능동적으로 다루는 4가지 능력.
❌ ① delete and remove: 삭제는 디지털 리터러시의 정의 아님.
❌ ② passively receive: 수동적 수용은 올바른 활용이 아님.
❌ ④ restrict and limit: 접근 제한은 디지털 리터러시 정의 아님.
det.tip: digital literacy = 정보를 찾고(find), 평가하고(evaluate), 만들고(create), 전달하는(communicate) 능력.

questions.passage: Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage. However, false information can __________ people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can stir up hatred against that group. It can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, misleading online reviews about questionable products often trick people into wasting money.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: cause emotional or financial harm to

det.korean: 허위 정보는 사람들에게 감정적 또는 재정적 피해를 줄 수 있다. 뒤에 이어지는 구체적 예시(증오, 싸움, 돈 낭비)가 근거.
det.analysis:
✅ ① cause emotional or financial harm to: 원문 직접 인용 + 뒤 예시(hatred, fights, wasting money)가 뒷받침.
❌ ② provide accurate: 허위정보의 피해 맥락에 정확한 정보 제공은 부적절.
❌ ③ build communities: 공동체 강화가 아닌 갈등 유발 맥락.
❌ ④ increase literacy: 디지털 리터러시 증가는 허위정보의 결과 아님.
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 예시(hatred, fights, wasting money)가 힌트. 모두 harm(피해)의 구체적 사례.

questions.passage: British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. He created a fake restaurant called The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and wrote it was reservations only. He did this to make people think The Shed was a special restaurant.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: The Shed는 누구나 방문 가능한 레스토랑이었다.
Butler는 The Shed가 특별한 곳이라고 생각하게 만들려 했다.

det.korean: 원문: 'He did this to make people think The Shed was a special restaurant.' Butler는 사람들이 특별한 레스토랑이라고 생각하게 만들려 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 특별한 곳이라고 생각하게: 원문 직접 일치.
❌ ① 실제 운영: fake restaurant — 가짜.
❌ ② 정확한 주소: did not provide an exact address.
❌ ③ 누구나 방문: reservations only — 예약 전용.
det.tip: 내용일치 문제: fake = 가짜, reservations only = 예약 전용. 세부 사실 확인 필수.

questions.passage: Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 식품 공급업체들이 The Shed에 무료 샘플을 보냈다.
Butler는 실제로 여러 끼의 식사를 제공했다.

det.korean: 원문: 'without Butler serving a single meal' — Butler는 단 한 끼도 제공하지 않았다. '여러 끼' 제공은 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 여러 끼 제공: 원문은 without serving a single meal(단 한 끼도 안 함). 불일치.
❌ ① 무료 샘플: sent him free samples. 일치.
❌ ③ 런던 1위: became London's number-one restaurant. 일치.
❌ ④ 2주 유지: held that ranking for two weeks. 일치.
det.tip: without + V-ing = ~하지 않고. without serving a single meal = 단 한 끼도 제공하지 않고.

questions.passage: You should then check the credibility of the content creator. If a story has no writer's name, this could be a sign that its content is questionable. If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before. If the person has not written anything else or writes for a website that looks unreliable, think twice before believing the content.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 작성자 이름이 없으면 내용이 신뢰할 만하다.
작성자가 다른 글을 쓴 적 없어도 믿을 수 있다.
이름이 있으면 그 사람이 이전에 어디서 보도했는지 알아봐야 한다.
신뢰할 수 없는 웹사이트에서 글을 써도 문제없다.

det.korean: 원문: 'If there is a name, find out what and where the person has reported before.' 이름이 있으면 이전 보도 이력을 확인해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 이전 보도 이력 확인: 원문 직접 일치.
❌ ① 이름 없으면 신뢰: 반대 — no writer's name = questionable.
❌ ② 다른 글 없어도 신뢰: 반대 — has not written anything else = think twice.
❌ ④ 문제없다: 반대 — unreliable website = think twice.
det.tip: credibility(신뢰성) 확인 3단계: 이름 유무 → 이전 보도 이력 → 웹사이트 신뢰성.

questions.passage: Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 허위 정보를 판별하기 위한 디지털 리터러시의 중요성

det.korean: 글 전체의 핵심: 디지털 리터러시(digital literacy)를 통해 온라인 허위 정보를 판별하는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 디지털 리터러시의 중요성: digital literacy, detect false information — 글의 핵심 메시지.
❌ ① 가짜 레스토랑 방법: Butler의 실험은 소재, 주제 아님.
❌ ③ 경제적 영향: 부분적 언급(wasting money)이지 주제 아님.
❌ ④ 인터넷 사용 감소: 올바른 사용법이지 사용 감소 아님.
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 메시지. digital literacy가 반복 키워드.

questions.passage: Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Digital Literacy: Your Shield Against False Information
How to Create a Successful Fake Restaurant
The Rise of Online Review Platforms
Why We Should Stop Using the Internet

det.korean: 디지털 리터러시: 허위 정보에 대한 방패. 허위 정보를 인식하고 피하는 능력의 중요성.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Digital Literacy: Shield: 글 전체 주제 — 디지털 리터러시로 허위 정보 방어.
❌ ② Fake Restaurant: 소재일 뿐 주제 아님.
❌ ③ Review Platforms: 리뷰 플랫폼 자체가 주제 아님.
❌ ④ Stop Using Internet: 사용 중단이 아닌 비판적 활용.
det.tip: 제목 = 주제를 함축적으로 표현. false information + digital literacy = 방어의 핵심.

questions.passage: Things quickly got, in Butler's words, <u>"a little out of hand."</u> From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. Interest further increased when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "a little out of hand"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 실험이 실패하여 결과를 얻지 못했다는 뜻
레스토랑 운영이 손이 부족할 만큼 바빠졌다는 뜻
상황이 예상을 넘어 통제할 수 없을 정도로 커졌다는 뜻

det.korean: "약간 걷잡을 수 없게 되었다" = 상황이 예상을 넘어 통제할 수 없을 정도로 커졌다. 최하위에서 1위까지 올라간 상황.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 예상을 넘어 통제 불가: out of hand = 통제 불능. 최하위→1위, 예약 전화, 무료 샘플 등 예상 밖 상황.
❌ ① 실험 실패: 오히려 '성공'이 과도했음.
❌ ② 손 부족: out of hand의 문자적 해석. 실제 레스토랑 아님.
❌ ④ 실험 중단: 중단 언급 없음. 계속 진행됨.
det.tip: out of hand = 통제를 벗어난, 걷잡을 수 없는. 관용적 표현.

questions.passage: He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site. Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed continuously climbed the London rankings. <u>He</u> started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 He가 가리키는 사람으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 He = Oobah Butler. The Shed라는 가짜 레스토랑을 만든 장본인으로, 예약 요청 이메일과 전화를 받은 사람.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Oobah Butler: 문단 전체의 주어. He faked → He asked → He started.
❌ ① 실제 요리사: The Shed에 실제 요리사 없음.
❌ ② 사이트 운영자: 언급 없음.
❌ ③ 친구: 리뷰를 쓴 사람이지 이메일 받은 사람 아님.
det.tip: 대명사 He의 지칭: 문맥상 The Shed를 만들고 운영한 Butler.

questions.passage: Fortunately, The Shed incident was an experiment that caused little damage. However, false information can cause emotional or financial harm to people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can stir up hatred against that group. <u>It</u> can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, misleading online reviews about questionable products often trick people into wasting money.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 It이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 특정 집단에 대한 허위 정보 (false information about a group)
특정 성별이나 신념 집단 (a gender or belief group)

det.korean: 밑줄 친 It = 특정 집단에 대한 허위 정보(false information about a certain gender or belief group). 이것이 집단 간 싸움을 유발한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 허위 정보: 앞 문장의 주어 false information을 받음. It = false information.
❌ ② 집단 자체: 집단이 싸움을 유발하는 것이 아님.
❌ ③ 온라인 리뷰: 다음 문장에서 별도로 언급.
❌ ④ 의심스러운 제품: 다음 문장에서 별도로 언급.
det.tip: 대명사 It: 앞 문장의 주어 false information을 받는다.

questions.passage: He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write favorable fake reviews on the review site.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Butler는 면도 크림, 미백 정제, 심지어 자기 발까지 사용하여 The Shed의 음식 사진을 __________했다."

(한 단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'He faked photos of The Shed's food' — 음식 사진을 위조했다.
det.analysis: ✅ faked: 원문에서 직접 찾기. faked photos = 사진을 위조했다.
det.tip: fake(위조하다): 가짜로 만들다. faked photos = 위조된 사진.

questions.passage: To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

We need to develop the ability to detect __________ (deceive) information.

(한 단어)

det.korean: detect + __________ + information → 명사 앞 형용사 자리. deceive(동사) → deceptive(형용사: 기만적인).
det.analysis: ✅ deceptive: 형용사 자리. deceive(동사) → deceptive(형용사). deceptive information = 기만적인 정보.
det.tip: deceive(동사: 속이다) → deceptive(형용사: 기만적인) → deception(명사: 기만).

questions.passage: Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is challenging. However, __________. The better we recognize false information, the better we will be at avoiding it and helping others do the same.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ it / is / important / that / we / know / what / false information / is / and / how / it / spreads ]
questions.wa: it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads
accept: it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads
It is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads
it is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads.
It is important that we know what false information is and how it spreads.

det.korean: 허위 정보가 무엇이고 어떻게 퍼지는지 아는 것이 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ it is important that(가주어-진주어) + we know(주절) + what false information is(간접의문문) + and how it spreads(병렬).
det.tip: it is important that ~: ~하는 것이 중요하다. what ... is + how ... spreads = 간접의문문 병렬.

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"그는 정확한 주소를 제공하지 않았다."

→ He did not provide an __________ address.

(한 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'He did not provide an exact address.' — 정확한 주소를 제공하지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ exact: 원문 직접 인용. an exact address = 정확한 주소.
det.tip: exact(정확한): exact address = 정확한 주소. provide = 제공하다.

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"허위 정보에 속지 않기 위해, 우리는 비판적으로 평가하는 습관을 길러야 한다."

→ To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of __________ evaluating what we see online.

(한 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'develop a habit of critically evaluating what we see online.' — 비판적으로 평가하는 습관.
det.analysis: ✅ critically: 원문 직접 인용. critically evaluating = 비판적으로 평가하는.
det.tip: critically(부사: 비판적으로). critical(형용사) → critically(부사). evaluating을 수식.
